courses.course_name: WorkSafeBC Occupational First Aid Level One
courses.course_overview_raw: A basic one day/8 hour course covering the essential ABC's - airway, breathing and circulation. How to deal with obstructed airways, breathing distress and control bleeding. One person CPR, minor wound care and records / reports are also part of the course. A 3 year certificate will be issued at the end of the course upon successful completion. Prerequisite(s): 16 years of age.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Students will have an opportunity to earn recognized workforce certificates (subject to availability); Fall Protection, Confined Space Entry and Stand by Attendant, Lift Truck Operator, Mobile Elevated Work Platform. Students must earn at least three workforce certificates. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

This course is an overview of interpreting and sketching blueprints. Students will be able to identify the alphabet lines, explain the three most commonly used orthographic views, use isometric drawings, working drawings, and make three way sketches of simple objects. The course includes lecture, as well assignments and quizzes. Prerequisite(s): Entry in to Trades Discovery

A key component of the program is an integrated trade’s research project directed by the student within their chosen field or industry: their own search for knowledge, expertise and individual contacts allows the student the opportunity to realistically assess the actuality of their educational and/or employment choice. Comparison studies reveal the complexities of the market trends and their impact and response to external and economic pressures. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to complete a market research paper on their chosen trade. Students will develop a job search portfolio that includes “blue collar” resume, cover letter and reference statements. Effective and efficient communication skills are essential elements in acquiring and retaining a career in a highly competitive job market environment. This course is designed to increase a student’s ability to prepare and practice for trade specific job applications and interview processes. Prerequisite(s): Entry in to Trades Discovery

courses.prerequisite_raw: Students failing TEXP 1150 Safe Work Practices, TEXP 1120 Career Preparation and/or 1 or more courses in Trades Discovery will not be allowed to participate in the TEXP 1130 Work Experience.
courses.course_overview_raw: Trades Discovery students participate in an approved unpaid work experience module. The work experience component ensures each student experiences first-hand the day- to- day realities of the work situation. Industry Tours/Lectures are scheduled to provide a bigger picture of the needs of Industry and possible opportunities for employment. Prerequisite(s): Students failing TEXP 1150 Safe Work Practices, TEXP 1120 Career Preparation and/or 1 or more courses in Trades Discovery will not be allowed to participate in the TEXP 1130 Work Experience.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Entry in to Trades Discovery – Must pass an Oxygen and Acetylene Safety Exam prior to any shop/practical work
courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers the operation of oxy-acetylene torches, including safety, ignition, flame types, shut down and storage of equipment. Applications of the oxy-acetylene torch for heating, cutting and welding will be covered during practical exercises. Sessions will include an introduction to SMAW (Shielded Metal Arc Welding) and MIG (Metal Inert Gas) welding. This course includes assignments, homework, and tests. Prerequisite(s): Entry in to Trades Discovery – Must pass an Oxygen and Acetylene Safety Exam prior to any shop/practical work

A series of in class sessions as well hands on in the shop training that encompass approximately twenty different Trades Training/Technical Studies programs taught at BCIT campuses. Lessons in safety, care and use of hand tools, power tools, and shop machinery will be taught and Applied Science will be covered. Students are placed in a workshop environment with a journeyed instructor where they will perform a number of tasks to gain experience in each trade. Each area will include an overview of the industry covering, apprenticeship and career opportunities. Prerequisite(s): Entry in to Trades Discovery

This course consists of sessions in applied basic mathematics; students are expected to complete math assignments in the following areas: whole numbers, fractions, decimals, measurements, ratios, conversions, percentage, exponents, equations, perimeter, area, volume and geometry. Students are required to complete hands-on applied math sessions as well as self-paced assignments and tests. Prerequisite(s): Entry in to Trades Discovery

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides an overview of WorkSafeBC and how Workers Compensation Regulations apply to industry. An in-depth look into safety culture in the workplace; focusing on safety precautions and procedures. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes January, May, and September each year *Scheduled intakes are subject to change Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program: BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment Visit the Trades Access website for samples of the Trades Entry Assessment. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Potential students with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963. Telephone interview is acceptable for out-of-town applicants. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
